Moses begged God to go with him and the people to the promised land. In these verses, the word *Presence* usually translates a Hebrew word that literally means “face” ({{Exodus 33:14-15|33:14–15}}). 

Earlier in the chapter, we learn that the Lord spoke with Moses "face to face" ({{Exodus 33:11|33:11}}). This phrase describes a close and direct relationship. It does not mean that Moses saw God’s physical face. It means that God spoke with Moses in a clear and personal way.

Moses wanted that same close relationship to continue. He did not want God to send only an angel or messenger. He wanted God’s own presence to go with them. Moses also wanted the people to share in that relationship in some way.

- *please let me know Your ways:* Moses did not just want God's blessings. He wanted to understand God's nature and character. He also wanted to know why and how God acted. God's goal of revealing himself was starting to happen, at least with Moses. 

- Moses wanted God to accompany them because they were the Lord's own people.
*I will give you rest*: Literally *a place to roost,* as in a place where a bird can land and be at peace. Ever since Abraham left Ur, he and his descendants had had no such place.

Moses made his request more direct. He showed he understood God's actions. The exodus was not just about leaving Egypt for Canaan. It was about experiencing God personally, which would change their lives. Without this, staying at Mount Sinai would have been better. Going to Canaan without the Lord would be disastrous.
The Lord reaffirmed his agreement to go with them and his personal appointment of Moses.

Moses asked for confirmation of God’s promises. He asked to see God’s glorious presence (literally *glory*). He was asking for an experience of seeing the very essence of God (see study note on 16:7).

- In his positive reply, God changed the terms of the request Moses made. God promised Moses a glorious experience, but he would not let Moses see his face. In the Old Testament, seeing God’s face means seeing God fully and directly.

Instead, God said he would show Moses his goodness. He would also proclaim his name. In the Bible, a name often expresses a person’s character and identity. God’s character is shown especially in his mercy and compassion (see {{Romans 9:14-16|Romans 9:14–16}}). 

- *the LORD*: In many English Bibles, the word LORD (written in capital letters) stands for the personal name of God, *Yahweh*. 

In this verse, God emphasizes his personal name. This name shows that he is not distant. He is the covenant God (the God who makes promises) of his people.

God desires to reveal his character to his people. However, to see his face means to see his full being (his true and complete nature). No human can see God in this way and live.

God’s glorious presence is described in {{Exodus 33:22|33:22}}. That kind of direct encounter would bring death to a human person. God allowed Moses to see only a small part of his glory. Moses was given a brief glimpse, but nothing more.

God called Moses to come back up Mount Sinai with two new stone tablets. The restrictions for the rest of the people are like those made at first (see {{Exodus 19:12-13|19:12–13}}, {{Exodus 19:21-25|21–25}}).

God granted the request of Moses ({{Exodus 33:18|33:18}}). He showed Moses his goodness ({{Exodus 34:1-9|34:1–9}}). He renewed the covenant ({{Exodus 34:10-35|34:10–35}}). 

This renewal was a statement made by God alone. God promised to stay with his people, keeping his covenant promises even though they had broken the covenant and deserved death and abandonment ({{Exodus 32:1-6|32:1–6}}).

*the LORD*: This represents the personal name of God, *Yahweh*. This name appears five times in this passage. By repeating this name, God emphasizes his personal name. This shows that he is speaking and acting as the covenant God (the God who makes promises) of his people.
Moses experienced God’s presence in a revelation of the name, or character, of God. As God had promised ({{Exodus 33:19|33:19}}), he showed Moses the glory of his goodness.

*compassionate and gracious* (see {{Exodus 20:5-6|20:5–6}}; {{Exodus 33:19|33:19}} and study notes): The Creator who was revealing himself to the Israelites, and through them to the world, is a God of grace. Neither his justice nor his sovereignty are underlined here, as true as those attributes are. If God were merely just, the Old Testament would have ended at this point, or it would have picked up and started again with an entirely new family. 

This did not happen because God, in his unique character, is slow to anger and full of unfailing love and faithfulness. These qualities were the basis for his renewal of the covenant.

- God’s unfailing love and his generous desire to forgive are not weakness or indecisiveness, nor are they reason to sin. Sin will have its effects, because God created a world of cause and effect. The murderer may repent, be forgiven, and lead a new life, but the effects of previous choices will continue to play out. We should not sin just because we know that God will forgive (see study note on 20:5–6). 

- *a thousand generations:* See {{Deuteronomy 7:9-11|Deuteronomy 7:9–11}}. 

- *He will visit the iniquity of the fathers: *Our sins affect future generations, but God limits the effects to three or four generations. See also {{Exodus 20:5-6|Exodus 20:5–6}}.

Since the Lord had already twice promised to go with them ({{Exodus 33:14|33:14}}, {{Exodus 33:17|17}})this renewed request seems to show a lack of faith. It may also be that God’s presence had driven home to Moses how absolutely holy God is and how very different he is from this stubborn and rebellious people. 

Here, Moses took his request a step further and asked God to travel with the people and make them his own treasured possession (see {{Exodus 19:5-6|19:5–6}}). Moses asked for the complete restoration of the relationship.

God promised to miraculously care for his people as he brought them into Canaan. This care depended on their obedience. In Hebrew, the word translated as *observe* also means "obey" ({{Exodus 34:11|34:11}}). Unlike English, Hebrew does not separate hearing a command from obeying it.
Some of the terms of the covenant are restated, particularly those that prohibit the worship of other gods and that describe the proper worship of the Lord.

Worship of idols was prohibited, particularly the idols of the peoples into whose lands the Israelites were going. A key part of this restriction was the ban on treaties, or covenants, with these idol-worshiping peoples. Making a treaty would mean acknowledging their gods, as ancient treaties often called upon gods as witnesses (see study note on 20:1–23:33). 

The treaties would also tempt the Israelites to adopt the customs of their treaty partners ({{Exodus 34:12|34:12}}, {{Exodus 34:15-16|15–16}}).

- Asherah was a Canaanite fertility goddess who would continue to be a temptation throughout Israel’s history (see, for example, {{Judges 6:25|Judges 6:25}}; {{1 Kings 14:15|1 Kings 14:15}}; {{2 Kings 23:15|2 Kings 23:15}}). 

- The Aherah poles seem to have been fertility symbols.

Marriage with people who worshiped other gods was a problem throughout the Old Testament. God warned His people not to marry those who followed other gods (see {{Genesis 24:3|Genesis 24:3}}; {{Ezra 9:1-2|Ezra 9:1–2}}; compare {{2 Corinthians 6:14-18|2 Corinthians 6:14–18}}).
*Feast of Ingathering:* See study notes on 23:16; Leviticus 23:15–21, 34–43.
*no one will covet your land:* If Israel would trust God and obey him, he would protect them.

Moses wrote down these repeated instructions that explained the main terms of the covenant ({{Exodus 34:27|34:27}}).

The Ten Commandments, which summarize these terms, were written on the new stone tablets ({{Exodus 34:28|34:28}}).
Moses, who had asked to see the glory of God, was not aware that his own face reflected that glory.

*he put a veil over his face:* While Moses was reporting what God had said to him, he left his face unveiled. Then he covered it, perhaps because of the fear its brightness caused during normal conversation ({{Exodus 34:30|34:30}}; see {{2 Corinthians 3:7-18|2 Corinthians 3:7–18}} for the apostle Paul's thoughts on this event).

Moses came down from Mount Sinai with stone tablets a second time. That time the Israelites listened and obeyed. Moses taught them to work for six days and to rest on the Sabbath day.

Then the entire community worked to make everything that God had told them to make. People freely gave offerings from what they had. Bezalel, Oholiab and other skilled workers used the offerings. They used them to make the holy tent and everything in it. They also made the priests’ clothes.

The Israelites made everything just as God had commanded Moses. Then Moses blessed the people. This was like when God created the world. He was pleased at what he had made and he blessed it (Genesis chapter 1).

When the holy tent was ready, God’s glory filled it. This showed that God was present with the Israelites in the tent. God continued to lead the people through the cloud and fire.

Much of the report about building the Tent of Meeting repeats what {{Exodus 25:1-31:18|25:1–31:18}} said. There is a change from the imperative mood to the indicative, and there are certain changes in the order. 

This repetition emphasizes that the work was done exactly as God commanded (see {{Exodus 40:16|40:16}}). The people had tried to secure God's presence their own way with the gold calf, which led to disaster. Now, by following God's way, they received blessings ({{Exodus 40:34-38|40:34–38}}).

At the creation of the gold calf, Aaron asked only for earrings (see study note on 32:2–4). Here, Moses invites the people to bring various gifts ({{Exodus 35:4-9|35:4–9}}). They gave as their hearts and spirits inspired them ({{Exodus 35:21|35:21}}). Everyone could contribute something and the giving was voluntary. So, the people ended up giving too much and Moses had to stop them ({{Exodus 36:4-7|36:4–7}}).

It says that Bezalel made the ark of the covenant and all the furnishings, as well as the courtyard and its furnishings ({{Exodus 37:1|37:1}}, {{Exodus 37:10|10}}, {{Exodus 37:17|17}}, {{Exodus 37:25|25}}; {{Exodus 38:1|38:1}}, {{Exodus 38:8|8}}, {{Exodus 38:9|9}}, {{Exodus 38:18|18}}). But this probably means he was in charge and guided the other craftsmen and seamstresses.

This section reports on building the courtyard ({{Exodus 38:9-20|38:9–20}}) and its equipment, including the altar of burnt offering and the bronze basin ({{Exodus 38:1-7|38:1–7}}; {{Exodus 38:8|38:8}}).

- The plans for the bronze basin were part of the instructions to the priests ({{Exodus 30:17-21|30:17–21}}; {{Exodus 29:38-30:38|29:38–30:38}}). Here, however, the text reports how the basin was built, following a logical order.

- This bronze, which they could polish to look like mirrors, was probably of very high quality. It was suitable for use in God's Tent of Meeting.
Since the tabernacle contained the ark of the covenant (also called the ark of the Testimony), it is called the *tabernacle of the Testimony*.

The very large amount of metal listed here includes more than one metric ton (about 1,000 kilograms) of gold, almost four metric tons (about 4,000 kilograms) of silver, and two and a half metric tons (about 2,500 kilograms) of bronze.

This large supply shows how eager the Egyptians were to send the Israelites away. The Egyptians gave the Israelites whatever they asked for so that they would leave quickly (see {{Exodus 12:35-36|12:35–36}}).

- For the earlier discussion of this tax, see {{Exodus 30:11-16|30:11–16}}. The *sanctuary shekel* was the standard used to measure other weights accurately. 

- *603,550:* See study note on 12:37.
The term *holy crown* might be a formal title. The initial description of the plate in {{Exodus 28:36|28:36}}does not include that term.

Moses inspected the completed work and confirmed that everything was as the Lord had commanded ({{Exodus 39:43|39:43}}). As a result, Moses blessed them instead of judging them. This was unlike when they tried to enter God's presence in their own ways ({{Exodus 32:27|32:27}}).

- The report on setting up the Tent of Meeting starts with the Lord's commands ({{Exodus 40:1-15|40:1–15}}). It continues with how Moses obeyed those commands ({{Exodus 40:16-33|40:16–33}}). 

- The repeated statement that "Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded" ({{Exodus 40:16|40:16}}, {{Exodus 40:19|19}}, {{Exodus 40:21|21}}, {{Exodus 40:23|23}}, {{Exodus 40:25|25}}, {{Exodus 40:27|27}}, {{Exodus 40:29|29}}, {{Exodus 40:32|32}}) strongly contrasts with Aaron’s self-serving statement in {{Exodus 32:22-24|32:22–24}}. God wants to share his presence with us, but his holiness requires us to give up our own efforts to secure his presence and gifts.

- In the Tent of Meeting, God met with Israel to communicate his will to them. 

- On the first day of the new year, they set up the Tent of Meeting. This was one year after God announced the Passover and the beginning of Israel's calendar.

*Testimony* (Hebrew *‘eduth*): This word refers especially to the covenant laws (stipulations, meaning the required commands).

A written copy of these laws was placed inside the ark. This copy served as a witness to the covenant that Israel had made with God.

*So Moses finished the work*: This statement marks the completion of the work on the tabernacle. The long process of building and preparing all its parts had now come to an end. See study note on 37:1–29.

The most important part of the exodus happened when the glory of the Lord filled the Tent of Meeting.

From the beginning, God’s purpose was not only to rescue Israel from slavery. He wanted to bring them into a close relationship with himself. Their greatest need was to know God personally.

Without God’s presence, the promised land would not truly be a place of blessing. But now it would be different. The same glory that appeared on Mount Sinai was now with Israel. It would not stay behind. It would travel with them wherever they went.

*all the house of Israel: *This description reminds us of how the book of Exodus began (see {{Exodus 1:1-7|1:1–7}}). At that time, Jacob’s family had grown into a large group in Egypt. Later, they became slaves there. This was a dramatic change. They were no longer slaves. Now they were free.

God had promised Abraham that his descendants would bring blessing to all the nations ({{Genesis 12:3|Genesis 12:3}}).

Therefore did Pharoh, king of Mizraim, give counsel to the Jehudith midwives, the name of one of whom was Shifra, who is Jokeved, and the name of the other Puvah, who is Miriam her daughter.
1:16: He said, “When you deliver Hebrew women, you must look at the birthstool. If it is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, let her live.”
And he said, When you attend Jehudith women, and see them bear, if it be a male child, you shall kill him; but if a daughter, you may let her live.
1:17: The midwives [however] feared [from before] Elohim and did not do as the Egyptian king had told them, and they kept the infant boys alive.
But the midwives feared before the Lord, and would not do according to what the king of Mizraim had said to them, but they saved the children.
1:18: The king of Egypt called for the midwives and said to them, “Why did you do this? You let the infant boys live.”
And the king of Mizraim called the midwives, and said to them, Why have you done this thing, and have saved the children?
1:19: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptians. They know how to deliver. Even before a midwife gets to them, they have already given birth.”

And the mid-wives said to Pharoh, The Jehudith women are not as the Mizraite, for they are sturdy (or, courageous) and wise-minded: before the midwife cometh to them they lift up their eyes in prayer, supplicating mercy before their Father who is in heaven, who heareth the voice of their prayer, and at once they are heard, and bring forth, and are delivered in peace.
1:20: Elohim was good to the midwives, and the people increased and were very mighty.
And the Lord did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and prevailed greatly.
1:21: Because the midwives feared [from before] God, He gave them houses.

And forasmuch as the midwives feared before the Lord, they obtained for themselves a good name unto the ages; and the Word of the Lord up-builded for them a royal house, even the house of the high priesthood.
1:22: Pharaoh then commanded all his people, saying, “Every boy who is born [to the Hebrews] must be thrown into the river; but every girl shall be allowed to live.”
But when Pharoh saw this, he commanded all his people, saying, Every male child that is born to the Jehudaee you shall cast into the river; but every daughter you may spare.
2:1: A man of the house of Levi went and married the daughter of Levi.

And Amram, a man of the tribe of Levi, went and returned to live in marriage with Jokeved his wife, whom he had put away on account of the decree of Pharoh. And she was the daughter of a hundred and thirty years when he returned to her; but a miracle was wrought in her, and she returned unto youth as she was, when in her minority she was called the daughter of Levi.
2:2: The woman conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was [exceptionally] good, and she kept him hidden for three months.
And the woman conceived and bare a son at the end of six months; and she saw him to be a child of steadfastness, (or, of steadfast life,) and hid him three months, which made the number nine.
2:3: When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus box and coated it with clay and tar. She placed the child in it, and placed it in the reeds near the bank of the river.

But she could conceal him no longer, for the Mizraee had become aware of him. And she took an ark of papyrus, (tunes,) and coated it with bitumen and pitch, and placed the child within it, and laid him among the reeds on the bank of the river.
2:4: [The child’s] sister stood herself at a distance to see what would happen to him.
And Miriam his sister stood at a distance to take knowledge of what would be done to him.
2:5: Pharaoh’s daughter went down to bathe by the river, while her maids walked along the river’s edge. She saw the box among the reeds and sent her maid and she fetched it.

And the Word of the Lord sent forth a burning sore and inflammation of the flesh upon the land of Mizraim; and the daughter of Pharoh came down to refresh herself at the river. And her handmaids, walking upon the bank of the river, saw the ark among the reeds, and put forth the arm and took it, and were immediately healed of the burning and inflammation.
2:6: She opened it and saw the child, and behold a boy was crying. She took pity on it, and said, “This is one of the Hebrew boys.”
And she opened, and saw the child, and, behold, the babe wept; and she had compassion upon him, and said, This is one of the children of the Jehudaee.
2:7: [The infant’s] sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call to you a nursing [mother] from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
And his sister said to Pharoh's daughter, May I go and call for thee a nursing woman from the Jehudesses, to suckle the babe for thee?
2:8: “Go,” said Pharaoh’s daughter to her. The young girl went and called the child’s mother.
And Pharoh's daughter said, Go; and the damsel went and called the child's mother.
2:9: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her [the child’s mother], “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your fee.” The woman took the child and nursed it.
And the daughter of Pharoh said, Take this child and suckle it for me, and I will give thee thy wages And the woman took the child and suckled him.
2:10: When the child grew up, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moshe, for she said, “I drew him from the water.”
And the child grew, and was brought to Pharoh's daughter, and he was beloved by her as a son; and she called his name Mosheh, Because, said she, I drew him out of the water of the river.
2:11: It was in those days when Moshe was grown that he [began] to go out to his brethren, and he saw their burdens [hard labor]. [One day] he saw an Egyptian beating one of his Hebrew brethren.

And in those days when Mosheh was grown up, he went forth to his brethren, and saw the anguish of their souls, and the greatness of their toil. And he saw a Mizraite man strike a Jewish man of his brethren;
2:12: He [Moshe] looked all around and [when] he saw that no man was there [watching], he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.

and Mosheh turned, and considered in the wisdom of his mind, and understood that in no generation would there arise a proselyte from that Mizraite man, and that none of his children's children would ever be converted; and he smote the Mizraite, and buried him in the sand.
2:13: He went out the next day, and behold two Hebrew men were quarreling. And he said to the wicked one, “Why are you beating your friend?”

And he went out the second day, and looked; and, behold, Dathan and Abiram, men of the Jehudaee contended; and seeing Dathan put forth his hand against Abiram to smite him, he said to him, Wherefore dost thou smite thy companion?
2:14: He [the wicked one] said, “Who made you a man, officer and judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Moshe was frightened, and he said, “So [Certainly] the matter is known.”

And Dathan said to him, Who is he who hath appointed thee a chief man and a judge over us? Wilt thou kill me, said he, as thou didst the Mizraite? And Mosheh was afraid, and said, Verily, the thing has become known.
2:15: Pharaoh heard about the matter, and he planned to kill Moshe. Moshe fled from Pharaoh, and resided in the land of Midian, and he sat [lived] near the well.
And Pharoh heard this thing, and sought to kill Mosheh; and Mosheh escaped before Pharoh, to dwell in the land of Midian. And he sat by a well.
2:16: The priest [minister] of Midian had seven daughters. They came to draw water [from the well] and fill the troughs to water their father’s sheep.
And the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came and drew, and filled the watering-troughs, to give drink to the flocks of their father.
2:17: Then the shepherds came and chased them away. Moshe got up and came to their aid, and then watered their sheep.
But the shepherds came and drave them away. And Mosheh arose in the power of his might, and rescued them, and gave the flocks drink.
2:18: When they came to Reu’eil, their father, he said [to them], “How did you get to come [home] so early today?”
And they came to Reuel, their grandfather, who said to them, How is it that you are come (so) early today?
2:19: They said, “An Egyptian rescued us from the hand of the shepherds; and he also drew [water] for us, and watered the sheep.”
And they replied, A Mizraite man not only delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, but also himself drawing drew and watered the flock.
2:20: He said to his daughters, “And where is he? Why did you abandon the man? Call him and let him eat bread.”
And he said to his son's daughters, And where is he? Why did you leave the man? Call him, and let him eat bread.
2:21: Moshe agreed to reside with the man, and he gave Moshe his daughter Tzipporah.

But when Reuel knew that Mosheh had fled from before Pharoh he cast him into a pit; but Zipporah, the daughter of his son, maintained him with food, secretly, for the time of ten years; and at the end of ten years brought him out of the pit. And Mosheh went into the bedchamber of Reuel, and gave thanks and prayed before the Lord, who by him would work miracles and mighty acts. And there was shown to him the Rod which was created between the evenings, and on which was engraven and set forth the Great and Glorious Name, with which he was to do the wonders in Mizraim, and to divide the sea of Suph, and to bring, forth water from the rock. And it was infixed in the midst of the chamber, and he stretched forth his hand at once and took it. Then, behold, Mosheh was willing to dwell with the man, and he gave Zipporah, the daughter of his son, to Mosheh.
2:22: When she gave birth to a son, he named him Gershom, for he said, “I have been a foreigner in a strange land.”
And she bare him a male child, and he called his name Gershom, Because, said he, a sojourner have I been in a strange land which is not mine.
2:23: A long time passed and the king of Egypt died. The B’nei Yisrael moaned because of their enslavement [which was hard upon them], and they cried. Their plea about their enslavement went up to [before] God.

And it was after many of those days that the king of Mizraim was struck (with disease), and he commanded to kill the firstborn of the sons of Israel, that he might bathe himself in their blood. And the sons of Israel groaned with the labour that was hard upon them; and they cried, and their cry ascended to the high heavens of the Lord. And He spake in His Word to deliver them from the travail.
2:24: Elohim heard their groaning [was heard before Elohim] and Elohim remembered His covenant with Avraham, with Yitzchok and with Yaakov.
And their cry was heard before the Lord, and before the Lord was the covenant remembered which He had covenanted with Abraham, with Izhak, and with Jakob.
2:25: Elohim saw [The enslavement of] the B’nei Yisrael [became revealed before Elohim], and Elohim took knowledge of them [said with His Word that He would deliver them].

And the Lord looked upon the affliction of the bondage of the sons of Israel; and the repentance was revealed before Him which they exercised in concealment, so as that no man knew that of his companion.
3:1: Moshe tended the sheep of his father-in-law Yisro, priest [minister] of Midian. He led the sheep to the edge of the wilderness [to the best pastures] and he came to the mountain [on which was the revealed the Glory] of God, in the area of Choreiv.

But Mosheh was keeping the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the rabba of Midian; and he had led the flock to a pleasant place of pasturage which is behind the desert, and had come to the mountain on which was revealed the glory of the Lord, even Horeb.
3:2: An angel of Adonoy appeared [became revealed] to him [Moshe] in the heart [a flame] of a fire in the midst of a thorn-bush. He looked and behold the bush was on fire, but the bush was not being consumed.

And Zagnugael, the angel of the Lord, appeared to him in a flame of fire in the midst of the bush. And he gazed, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, yet the bush was neither burned nor consumed with fire.
3:3: Moshe said, “I must turn aside and see [investigate] this great sight. Why doesn’t the bush burn?”
And Mosheh said, I will turn aside now and consider this great sight, why the bush is not burned.
3:4: When Adonoy saw that [Moshe] turned aside to see, Elohim called to him from the midst of the thorn-bush, and said, “Moshe, Moshe.’” He [Moshe] said, “Here I am.”
And when it was seen before the Lord that he turned to look, the Lord called to him from the midst of the bush and said, Mosheh, Mosheh ! And he said, Behold me.
3:5: He [God] said, “Do not come any closer. Take your shoes off your feet, because the place upon which you are standing is [a] holy ground [place].”
And He said, Approach not hither, take the shoe from thy feet, for the place on which thou standest is a holy place; and upon it thou art to receive the Law, to teach it to the sons of Israel.
3:6: He [God] then said, “I am the God of your father, the God of Avraham, the God of Yitzchok, and the God of Yaakov.” Moshe hid his face, for he was afraid to look at [the side of the Glory of] Elohim.

And He said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Izhak, and the God of Jakob. And Mosheh covered his face; for he was afraid to look upon the height of the glory of the Shekinah of the Lord.
3:7: Adonoy said, “I have indeed seen the suffering of My people that are in Egypt [has indeed been revealed before Me]. I have heard how they [Their] cry out [is heard before Me] because [of the harshness] of their slave-masters, and I am aware of their pain [has become revealed before Me].

And He said, The oppression of My people who are in Mizraim is verily manifest before Me, and heard before Me is their cry on account of them who hold them in bondage; for their affliction is known before Me.
3:8: I have descended [become revealed] to free them from the hand of Egypt, and to bring them up from that land to a good, spacious land, to a land flowing with [producing] milk and honey; to the territory of the Canaanites, the Chittites, the Emorites, the Perizites, the Chivites and the Yevusites.

And I have revealed Myself to thee this day, that by My Word they may be delivered from the hand of the Mizraee, to bring them up out of the unclean land, unto a good land, and large in its boundaries, a land yielding milk and honey, unto the place where dwell the Kenaanaee, and the Hittaee, and the Amoraee, and the Pherizaee, and the Hivaee, and the Jebusaee.
3:9: Now, behold, the cry of the B’nei Yisrael has come to [before] Me. I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them [is also revealed before Me].
And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel cometh up before Me, and the bruising of the Mizraee wherewith they bruise them is also revealed before Me.
3:10: Now go [come]. I am sending you to Pharaoh, and you will bring My people, the B’nei Yisrael, out of Egypt.”
And now, come, and I will send thee unto Pharoh, and thou shalt bring forth My people, the sons of Israel, out of Mizraim.
3:11: Moshe said to [before] Elohim, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh? Am I able to bring the B’nei Yisrael out of Egypt?”
And Mosheh said before the Lord, Who am I, that I should go to Pharoh, and bring forth the sons of Israel out of Mizraim?
3:12: He [God] said, “Because I will be with you [My Word will be your support]. This will be the proof that I have sent you—when you bring the people out of Egypt—you will serve [before] Elohim on this mountain.”

But He said, Therefore My Word shall be for thy help; and this shall be the sign to thee that I have sent thee: when thou hast, brought the people forth from Mizraim, ye shall worship before the Lord, because ye shall have received the Law upon this mountain.
3:13: Moshe said to [before] Elohim, “Behold, when I come to the B’nei Yisrael and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers sent me to you,’ they will say to me, ‘What is His name?’ What shall I say to them?”

And Mosheh said before the Lord, Behold, I will go to the sons of Israel, and say to them, The Lord God of your fathers hath sent me to you: and they will say to me, What is His Name ? What shall I say to them?
3:14: Elohim said to Moshe, “Eh’yeh Asher Eh’yeh;” and He said, “This is what you must say to the B’nei Yisrael, ‘Eh’yeh sent me to you.’”

And the Lord said unto Mosheh, He who spake, and the world was; who spake, and all things were. And He said, This thou shalt say to the sons of Israel, I AM HE WHO IS, AND WHO WILL BE, hath sent me unto you.
3:15: Elohim continued talking to Moshe, “This is what you must say to the B’nei Yisrael, ‘Adonoy, the God of your fathers, the God of Avraham, the God of Yitzchok, and the God of Yaakov, sent me to you. This is My eternal Name, and this is how I am to be mentioned for all generations.’”

And the Lord said again unto Mosheh, Thus shalt thou speak to the sons of Israel, The God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Izhak, and the God of Jakob, hath sent me unto you. This is His Name for ever, and this is His Memorial to every generation and generation.
3:16: “Go, gather the elders of Yisrael, and say to them, ‘Adonoy, the God of your fathers appeared [became revealed] to me—the God of Avraham, Yitzchok and Yaakov—saying, “I have indeed been mindful of you, regarding that which is being done to you in Egypt.

Go, and assemble the elders of Israel, and say to them, The Lord God of your fathers hath appeared unto me, the God of Abraham, Izhak, and Jakob, saying, Remembering, I have remembered you, and the injury that is done you in Mizraim;
3:17: I have said, I will bring you up out of the suffering of Egypt, to the land of the Canaanites, the Chittites, the Emorites, the Perizites, the Chivites and the Yevusites; to a land flowing with [producing] milk and honey.’”

and I have said in My Word, I will bring you up out from the oppression of the Mizraee into the land of the Kenaanaee, and Hittaee, and Amoraee, and Pherizaee, and Hivaee, and Jebusaee, to the land that yieldeth milk and honey.
3:18: They will listen to [obey] your voice [Words]. You and the elders of Yisrael will come to the king of Egypt, and say to him, ‘Adonoy, God of the Hebrews happened to meet with us. Now we request that you let us go [now] into the wilderness for three days, to bring an offering [sacrifice] to [before] Adonoy, our God.’

And they will hearken to thee: and thou and the elders of Israel shall go to the king of Mizraim and say to him, The Lord God of the Jehudaee hath called us; and now let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, to sacrifice before the Lord our God.
3:19: I know [It is revealed before Me] that the king of Egypt will not allow you to go [on this journey], but not because of his [power is] strong hand.
But it is manifest before Me that the king of Mizraim will not let you go, (no,) not from fear of Him who is Mighty, until that by My Word he shall have been punished with evil plagues.
3:20: I will then send forth my hand [the blow of My power], and strike Egypt with all My wondrous deeds that I will perform in their midst. Then he [Pharaoh] will send you out.
And ye will be hindered there until I have sent forth the stroke of My power, and have smitten Mizraee with all My wonders, that I will do among them; and afterward he will release you.
3:21: I will give this people grace in the eyes of the Egyptians; and when you go, you will not leave empty handed.
And I will give this people grace in the eyes of the Mizraee; and it shall be that when ye go free from thence, ye shall not go empty.
3:22: Every woman shall borrow from her neighbor, and from the woman living in her house, articles of silver and gold, and clothing. You shall put them on your sons and daughters, and thus you will divest Egypt of its wealth.”

But a woman shall ask of her neighbour, and from those next to the wall of her house, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vestments; and you shall set them as crowns upon your sons and your daughters, and make the Mizraee empty.
4:1: Moshe answered and said, “They will not believe me. They will not listen to my voice [obey me]. They will say, ‘Adonoy did not appear [become revealed] to you.’”
And Mosheh answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken to me; for they will say, The Lord hath not appeared to thee.
4:2: Adonoy said to him, “What is that in your hand?” He said, “A rod.”
And the Lord said to him, What is that in thy hand ? And he said, The rod.
4:3: [God] said, “Throw it on the ground.” He [Moshe] threw it on the ground and it turned into a snake. Moshe ran away from it.
And He said, Cast it on the ground; and he cast it to the ground, and it became a serpent; and Mosheh fled from before it.
4:4: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Reach out your hand and grasp its tail.” He reached out his hand and took hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand.
And the Lord said to Mosheh, Stretch forth thy hand and seize (it) by its tail. And he stretched forth his hand and grasped it, and it became the rod in his hand:
4:5: “This is so that they will believe that Adonoy appeared [became revealed] to you; the God of their fathers, God of Avraham, God of Yitzchok and God of Yaakov.”
In order that they may believe that the Lord God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Izhak, and the God of Jakob, hath revealed Himself to thee.
4:6: Adonoy said furthermore to him [Moshe], “Put your hand into your bosom.” He put his hand into his bosom, and when he withdrew it, his hand had become a snow-like tzora’as [white as snow].
And the Lord said to him again, Put now thy hand within thy breast (Choba); and he put it within his breast, and withdrew it, and, behold, his hand was leprous, it was white as snow.
4:7: He [Adonoy] said, “Put your hand into your bosom again.” [Moshe] put his hand into his bosom again, and when he withdrew it from his bosom, it had become [normal] as his flesh.
And He said, Return thy hand into thy bosom (Aitaph); and he returned his hand to his breast, and withdrew it from his breast, and it had become clean as his flesh.
4:8: “If they do not believe you, and they do not listen to [accept] the voice [of proof] of the first [miraculous] sign; then they will believe the voice [of proof] of the latter [second] sign.
4:9: And if they will not believe even these two signs, and they will not listen to your voice [accept you], then you shall take from the water of the river and pour it on the dry land. The water that you will take from the river will turn into blood on the dry land.”

And if they believe not these two signs, nor receive from thee, thou shalt take of the water of the river and pour it on the ground, and the water that thou shalt take from the river shall become blood upon the ground.
4:10: Moshe said to [before] Adonoy, “I beg You Adonoy, I am not a man of words—not since yesterday, not since the day before—not from the time You [first] spoke to Your servant, for I am clumsy [slow] of mouth [speech] [heavy of speech] and clumsy [slow] of tongue [language].”

And Mosheh said before the Lord, O Lord, I pray: I am not a man of words, nor ever have been before that Thou didst speak with Thy servant; for I am of a staggering * mouth and staggering speech. *Or, lame
4:11: Adonoy said to him, “Who gave man a mouth, or who makes [a person] dumb or deaf? [Who makes a person] see or makes him blind? Is it not I—Adonoy?”
And the Lord said, Who is he who first put the language of the mouth into the mouth of man? or who hath appointed the dumb or the deaf, the open-seeing or the blind, but I the Lord?
4:12: Now go. I [My Word] will be with your mouth, and teach you what to say.”
And now go, and I by My Word will be with the speaking of thy mouth, and will teach thee what thou shalt say.
4:13: [Moshe] said, “I beg You Adony [my Master,] please [now] send the one You usually send [who is fit to be sent].”
And he said, I pray for mercy before the Lord. Send now Thy sending by the hand of Phinehas, by whom it is to be sent at the end of the days.
4:14: Adonoy displayed anger toward Moshe and said, “Is not Aharon, the Levite, your brother? I know [It is revealed before Me] that he knows how to speak. Behold he is setting out to meet you, and when he sees you he will rejoice in his heart.

And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Mosheh, and He said, Is it not manifest before Me that Aharon thy brother speaking can speak? And, behold, also, he cometh forth to meet thee, and will see thee and rejoice in his heart.
4:15: You will speak to him and put the words in his mouth. I [My Word] will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you what to do.
And thou shalt speak with him, and put the matter in his mouth, and My Word shall be with the word of thy mouth, and with the word of his mouth, and I will instruct you what you are to do.
4:16: He will speak to the people for you. He will be your spokesman, and you will be his master.
And he shall speak for thee with the people, and be to thee an interpreter, and thou to him the principal, seeking instruction from before the Lord.
4:17: Take this rod in your hand, for with it you will perform the [miraculous] signs.”
And this rod take thou in thy hand to work therewith the signs.
4:18: Moshe went and returned to Yeser, his father-in-law, and said to him, “I would like to leave [now] and return to my brothers in Egypt, to see if they are still alive.” Yisro said to Moshe, “Go in peace.”
And Mosheh went, and returned unto Jethro his father in law, and said, I will now go to my brethren who are in Mizraim, to see how they now live. And Jethro said to Mosheh, Go in peace.
4:19: Adonoy said to Moshe in Midian, “Go, return to Egypt, for they have died—all the men who had sought your life [to kill you].”

And the Lord said unto Mosheh in Midian, Go, return to Mizraim; for they have come to nought, and gone down from their possessions; behold, all the men who sought to take thy life are reckoned as the dead.
4:20: Moshe [then] took his wife and his sons, set them to ride on the donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt. Moshe took the rod of [with which miracles had been carried out before] God in his hand.

And Mosheh took his wife and his sons, and made them ride on the ass, and returned to the land of Mizraim. And Mosheh took the rod which he had brought away from the chamber of his father-in-law; and it was from the sapphire Throne of glory, in weight forty sein; and upon it was engraven and set forth the Great and Glorious Name by which the signs should be wrought before the Lord by his hand.
4:21: Adonoy said to Moshe, “On your way back to Egypt, see [keep in mind] all the wondrous [signs] that I have placed in your hand, and do them before Pharaoh. I will harden his heart, and he will not send the people out.

And the Lord said to Mosheh, In going to return into Mizraim, consider all the miracles that I have put in thy hand, and do them before Pharoh: and I will make obstinate the disposition (passion) of his heart, and he will not deliver the people.
4:22: You will say to Pharaoh, This is what Adonoy said, Yisroel is My son, My firstborn.
And thou shalt say to Pharoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is My first-born son;
4:23: And I have said to you, send out My son and let him serve [before] Me. If you refuse to send him, behold, I will slay your [own] firstborn son.”
and to thee I say, Let My son go free, that he may worship before Me; and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy first-born son.
4:24: He [Moshe] was along the way, in the inn, [an Angel of] Adonoy confronted him, and wanted to kill him.

But it was on the way, in the place of lodging that the angel of the Lord met him, and sought to kill him, because Gershom his son had not been circumcised, inasmuch as Jethro his father-in-law had not permitted him to circumcise him: but Eliezer had been circumcised, by an agreement between them two.
4:25: Tzipporah took a flint-stone and cut off her son’s foreskin, and threw it at his feet [brought it before him], saying, “You are a bridegroom of blood to me [With this blood of circumcision, a husband is given to us].”

And Zipporah took a stone, and circumcised the foreskin of Gershom her son, and brought the severed part to the feet of the angel, the Destroyer, and said, The husband sought to circumcise, but the father-in-law obstructed him; and now let this blood of the circumcision atone for my husband.
4:26: He then withdrew from him [Moshe. Then she said, “[You are] a bridegroom of blood [to me] because of the circumcision [Were it not for this blood of circumcision, my husband would have deserved to be killed].”
And the destroying angel desisted from him, so that Zipporah gave thanks, and said, How lovely is the blood of this circumcision that hath delivered my husband from the angel of destruction!
4:27: Adonoy said to Aharon, “Go meet Moshe in the desert.” He [Aharon] went and met him at the mountain [upon which was revealed the Glory] of God and he kissed him.
And the Lord had said to Aharon, Go and meet Mosheh in the desert. And he came and met him at the mountain where was revealed the glory of the Lord, and he embraced him.
4:28: Moshe told Aharon all the words of Adonoy with which He had sent him; and all the [miraculous] signs that He had commanded him [to demonstrate].
And Mosheh delivered to Aharon all these words with which he had sent him, and all the signs that he had instructed him to work.
4:29: Moshe and Aharon went [to Egypt] and they gathered all the elders of the B’nei Yisrael.
And Mosheh and Aharon went, and gathered together all the elders of the sons of Israel.
4:30: Aharon spoke all the words that Adonoy had spoken to Moshe, and he demonstrated the [miraculous] signs in the eyes [sight] of the people.
And Aharon spake all the words which the Lord had spoken with Mosheh, and did the signs in the eyes of the people.
4:31: The people believed. When they heard that Adonoy was mindful of the B’nei Yisrael, and that He had seen their suffering [was revealed before Him], they bowed their heads and prostrated themselves.
And the people believed, and heard that the Lord had remembered the sons of Israel, and that their bondage was manifest before Him; and they bowed themselves and worshipped.
5:1: Afterwards Moshe and Aharon went and said to Pharaoh, “This is what Adonoy, God of Yisrael said, ‘Send My people, so they may celebrate a festival to [before] Me in the wilderness.”
And after this Mosheh and Aharon went in unto Pharoh, and said, Thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel: Release My people, that they may make unto Me a festival in the wilderness.
5:2: Pharaoh said, “Who is [The Name of] Adonoy [is not revealed to me] that I should obey his voice [Word], to let Yisrael go. I do not know [The Name of] Adonoy [is not revealed to me], nor will I let [the B’nei] Yisrael go.”

And Pharoh said, The name of the Lord is not made known to me, that I should receive His word to release Israel. I have not found written in the Book of the Angels the name of the Lord. Of Him I am not afraid, neither will I release Israel.
5:3: They said [to him], “The God of the Hebrews has revealed Himself to us. Please [Now] allow us to take a three day journey into the wilderness, and let us sacrifice to [before] Adonoy, our God, lest He strike us with the plague or with the sword.”

And they said, The Name of the God of the Jehudaee is invoked by (or upon) us. We will go, then, to proceed three days into the desert, and offer the sacrifices of a festival before the Lord God, that death and slaughter befall us not.
5:4: The king of Egypt said to them, “Why, Moshe and Aharon, are you distracting the people from their work? Get back to your burdens.”
And the king of Mizraim said to Mosheh and Aharon, Why do you make the people cease from their labours? Go to your work.
5:5: Then Pharaoh said, “Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you want them to take leave from their hard work.”
And Pharoh said, Behold, this people of the land are many, whom you would stop from their service.
5:6: That day, Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their officers, saying,
And Pharoh that day commanded the officers of the people and their exactors, saying,
5:7: “You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks as before. Let them go gather [their own] straw,
You shall no more give straw to the people to cast bricks as heretofore; let them go and collect straw for themselves;
5:8: [And] the quota of bricks that they made before, you shall place upon them; do not reduce it, for they are lazy and therefore they cry out, saying, ‘We want to go sacrifice to [before] our God.’

but the (same) number of bricks which they have heretofore made ye shall lay upon them, and not diminish from it, because they are idle; therefore they clamour, saying, Let us go to offer the sacrifice of a festival before our God.
5:9: Make the workload heavier on the men, and make them do it. Let them not talk about [be occupied with] false ideas.”
Make their work strenuous upon the men, that they may be occupied with it, and not be setting their hopes upon lying words.
5:10: They went out—the taskmasters of the people and their officers—and spoke to the people, saying, “This is what Pharaoh said, ‘I will no longer give you straw.
And the officers and exactors of the people went forth, and said to the people, Thus saith Pharoh, I will not give you straw;
5:11: You must go get your own straw wherever you can find it, but your workload must not be reduced.’”
you must go and take straw wherever you can find it; for your work will not in anywise be diminished.
5:12: The people spread out all over Egypt to gather grain-chaff for straw.
And the people were scattered abroad in all the land of Mizraim to gather stubble for the straw.
5:13: The taskmasters pressured them saying, “You must complete your daily work [quota], just as [you did] [before] when there was straw [given to you].”
But the officers were pressing, saying, Fulfil your work day by day, as you did when the straw was given you.
5:14: The officers of the B’nei Yisrael were beaten—those whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had appointed—and were told, “Why have you not completed your quotas of brick making as you did yesterday and before neither yesterday, nor today?”

And the exactors whom Pharoh set over them as officers beat the sons of Israel, saying, Why have not you fulfilled your appointment, to cast (the same number of) bricks as heretofore, today as yesterday?
5:15: The officers of the B’nei Yisrael came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying “Why are you doing this to your slaves?
And the foremen came, and cried before Pharoh, saying, Why hast thou dealt thus with thy servants?
5:16: Your slaves are not given straw, and yet we are told to make bricks. Your slaves are beaten, and it is a sin for your people [sin against them].”
Thou hast not given thy servants the straw, and (yet) say they to us, Make the bricks; and, behold, they beat thy servants, and the guilty treatment of thy people is strong, but it goeth up!
5:17: He said, “You are lazy, therefore you say, ‘Let us go sacrifice to [before] Adonoy.’
But he said, You are idle, idle: therefore you are saying, Let us go and over the sacrifice of a festival before our God.
5:18: Now go, get to work. You will not be given straw, and you must deliver your quota of bricks.”
And now, go, work; but the straw shall not be given you, yet the number of the bricks you shall produce.
5:19: The officers of the B’nei Yisrael realized their bad position, saying, “You must not reduce your daily quota of bricks.”
And the foremen of the sons of Israel saw that they were in evil, (in his) saying, Ye are not to withhold the assignment of your bricks from day to day.
5:20: They met Moshe and Aharon who were waiting to meet them as they were leaving Pharaoh.
And they met Mosheh and Aharon, who stood before them when they came out from the presence of Pharoh,
5:21: They said to them [Moshe and Aharon], “Let Adonoy look at [become revealed to] you and judge [take revenge]. You have made our aroma abhorrent in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, putting a sword in their hands to kill us.”

and they said to them, Our affliction is manifest before the Lord, but our punishment is from you who have made our smell offensive before Pharoh and his servants; for you have occasioned a sword to be put into their hand to kill us.
5:22: Moshe returned to [before] Adonoy and said, “My Master. Why have You brought harm to this people? Why did You send me?
And Mosheh returned before the Lord, and said, O Lord, why hast Thou done evil to this people, and wherefore hast Thou sent me?
5:23: Ever since I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your Name, he has done harm to this people; and You have not rescued Your people.”
From the hour that I went in unto Pharoh to speak in Thy name, this people hath suffered evil, and delivering Thou hast not delivered them.
6:1: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for by [My] strong hand he will let them go, and by [a] strong hand, he will drive them out of his land.”
And the Lord said unto Mosheh, Now have I seen what Pharoh hath done: for by a strong hand shall he release them, and with a strong hand drive them forth from his land.
6:2: Elohim spoke to Moshe and said to him, “I am Adonoy.
AND the Lord spake with Mosheh, and said to him, I am the Lord who revealed Myself to thee in the midst of the bush, and said to thee, I am the Lord.
6:3: I revealed Myself to Avraham, to Yitzchok, and to Yaakov as Almighty Shaddai, but My Name Adonoy I did not make known to them.
And I was revealed unto Abraham, and to Izhak, and to Jakob, as EI-Shaddai; but My Name Ye-ya, as it discovereth My Glory,* was not known to them. *Or, in the face of My Shekinah
6:4: I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojourning where they lived as strangers.
And I confirmed also My covenant with them, to give them the land of Kenaan, the land of their sojourning in which they were sojourners.
6:5: And also [before Me] I have heard the groaning of the B’nei Yisrael, that the Egyptians are enslaving them, [has been heard before Me] and I have remembered My covenant.
And now cometh before Me the groaning of the sons of Israel, because the Mizraee do enslave them; and I remember My covenant.
6:6: Therefore say to the B’nei Yisrael, ‘I am Adonoy. I will bring you out from under [amongst] the [heavy] burdens of Egypt [the Egyptians], and I will save you from their slavery. I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with acts of great judgments.

Therefore say to the sons of Israel, I am the Lord; and I will bring you forth from the oppressive bondage of the Mizraee, and will deliver you from your servitude, and save you with an uplifted arm, and by great judgments.
6:7: I will take [bring] you to Myself [before Me] as a people, and I will be to you Elohim. You will know that I am Adonoy, your God Who is bringing you out from under [amongst] the [heavy] burdens of Egypt.
And I will bring you nigh before Me to be a people, and I will be a God unto you, and you shall know that I am the Lord your God who hath led you forth from the hard service of the Mizraee.
6:8: I will bring you to the land regarding which I raised My hand [in oath] [swore with My Word] that I would give it to Avraham, Yitzchok and Yaakov, and I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am Adonoy.’”
And I will bring you into the land which I covenanted by My Word to give unto Abraham, to Izhak, and to Jakob; and I will give it to you for an inheritance. I Am the Lord.
6:9: Moshe spoke [these words] to the B’nei Yisrael, but they would not listen to [obey] Moshe because of [their] shortness of wind and [the] hard labor [that was hard upon them].
And Mosheh spake according to this to the sons of Israel; but they received not from Mosheh, through anxiety of spirit, and from the strange and hard service which was upon their hands.
6:10: And the Lord spake to Mosheh saying,
6:11: “Come, speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, that he send the B’nei Yisrael out of his land.”
Go in, speak with Pharoh, the king of Mizraim, that he release the children of Israel from his land.
6:12: Moshe spoke before Adonoy, saying, “Behold the B’nei Yisrael have not listened to [obeyed] me, how then will Pharaoh listen to [accept] me—I whose lips are covered [am heavy of speech].”
And Mosheh said before the Lord, Behold, the sons of Israel do not hearken to me; how then will Pharoh hearken to me, and I a man difficult of speech?
6:13: Adonoy [then] spoke to Moshe and Aharon, commanding them regarding the B’nei Yisrael and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to bring out the B’nei Yisrael from the land of Egypt.

And the Lord spake with Mosheh and with Aharon, and gave them admonition for the sons of Israel, and sent them to Pharoh, king of Mizraim, to send forth the children of Israel from the land of Mizraim.
6:14: These are the heads of their paternal households: the sons of Reuvein, the first-born of Yisrael [are]: Chanoch, Pallu, Chetzron and Carmi. These are the families of Reuvein.
These are the heads of the house of their fathers. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, Hanok and Phallu, Hezron and Karmi; these are the race of Reuben.
6:15: The sons of Shimon: Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yachin, Tzochar and Shaul, the son of the Canaanite woman. These are the families of Shimon.
And the sons of Shimeon, Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jakin, and Sochar, and Shaul (he is Zimri, who yielded himself unto fornication, as among the Kenaanaee); these are the race of Shimeon.
6:16: These are the names of the sons of Leivi, according to their generations: Gershon, Kehos, and Merari. The years of Leivi’s life were one hundred and thirty-seven years.

And these are the names of the sons of Levi, according to their race: Gershon, and Kehath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi a hundred and thirty and seven years: he lived to see Mosheh and Aharon the deliverers of Israel.
6:17: The sons of Gershon: Livni and Shimi, and their families [descending from them].
And the sons of Gershon, Libni and Shemei, according to their generations.
6:18: The sons of Kehos: Amram, Yitzhar, Chevron and Uzziel. The years of Kehos’s life were one hundred and thirty-three years.

And the sons of Kehath, Amram, and Jitshar, and Hebron, and Uzziel. And the years of the life of Kehath the saint, a hundred and thirty and three years. He lived to see Phinehas, who is Elijah, the Great Priest, who is to be sent to the captivity of Israel at the end of the days.
6:19: The sons of Merari: Machli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their [descending] generation.
And the sons of Merari, Mahali and Mushi; these are the race of Levi according to the generations.
6:20: Amram took his aunt [father’s sister] Yocheved for his wife and she bore him Aharon and Moshe. The years of Amram’s life were one hundred and thirty-seven years.

And Amram took Jokeved his cousin to wife, and she bare him Aharon and Mosheh; and the years of Amram the saint were a hundred and thirty and seven years. He lived to see the children of Rechabia bar Gershom bar Mosheh.
6:21: The sons of Yitzhar: Korach, Nefeg and Zichri.
And the sons of Jitshar (were) Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
6:22: The sons of Uzziel: Mishaeil, Eltzaphan and Sisri.
And the sons of Uzziel, Mishael, and Elsaphan, and Sithri.
6:23: Aharon took Elisheva, daughter of Aminadav, sister of Nachshon, for a wife, and she bore him Nadav, Avihu, Elazar and Isamar.
And Aharon took Elisheba, daughter of Aminadab, sister of Nachshon, Unto him to wife, and she bare him Nadab and Abihu, Elasar and Ithamar.
6:24: The sons of Korach: Assir, Elkanah and Aviasaf. These are the families of the Korachites.
And the sons of Korah, Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these are the race of Korah.
6:25: Elazar, son of Aharon took, for himself one of the daughters of Putieil, for a wife, and she bore him Pinchas. These are the heads of the Levites’ patriarchs according to their families.
And Elasar bar Aharon took unto him a wife from the daughters of Jethro who is Putiel, and she bare him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers of the Levites, according to their generations.
6:26: This is [the lineage of] Aharon and Moshe to whom Adonoy had said, “Bring the B’nei Yisrael out of the land of Egypt with their multitudes.”
These are Aharon and Mosheh, to whom the Lord said, Bring forth the sons of Israel free from the land of Mizraim, according to their hosts;
6:27: They are the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to bring the B’nei Yisrael out of Egypt. These are Moshe and Aharon.
-these are they who spake with Pharoh, king of Mizraim, that he should send out the sons of Israel from Mizraim; it is Mosheh the prophet, and Aharon the priest.
6:28: It was the day when Adonoy spoke to Moshe in the land of Egypt.
And it was in the day when the Lord spake with Mosheh in the land of Mizraim, that Aharon gave a listening ear, and heard what He spake with him.
6:29: Adonoy spoke to Moshe saying, “I am Adonoy. Speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, all that I am speaking to you.”
And the Lord spake with Mosheh, and said to him, I am the Lord. Say to Pharoh, king of Mizraim all that I tell thee.
6:30: Moshe said before Adonoy, “Behold, I have covered lips [am heavy of speech]. How will Pharaoh listen to [accept] me?”
And Mosheh said before the Lord, Behold, I am difficult in speaking; how then will Pharoh hearken to me?
7:1: Adonoy said to Moshe, “See, I have made [appointed] you a god [master] to Pharaoh, and Aharon, your brother will be your spokesman.
But the Lord said to Mosheh, Wherefore art thou fearful? Behold, I have set thee a terror to Pharoh, as if thou wast his God, and Aharon thy brother shall be thy prophet.
7:2: You will speak all that I command you and Aharon, your brother, will speak to Pharaoh, that he send the B’nei Yisrael out of his land.
Thou shalt speak to Aharon that which I command thee, and Aharon thy brother shall speak to Pharoh, that he release the sons of Israel from his land.
7:3: I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, [in order to] increase My signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
But I will harden the disposition of Pharoh's heart to multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Mizraim.
7:4: [Thus] Pharaoh will not listen to [accept] you. But then I will display My hand [the blow of My power] against Egypt, and I will bring My multitude, My people, the B’nei Yisrael out of the land of Egypt with great acts of judgment.
Nor will Pharoh hearken to you. But I will shoot among them the arrows of death, and inflict the plagues of My mighty hand upon Mizraim, and will bring out the sons of Israel free from among them.
7:5: Egypt will then know that I am Adonoy when I send forth My hand [the blow of My power] over Egypt and bring out the B’nei Yisrael from among them.”
7:6: Moshe and Aharon did so. They did exactly as Adonoy commanded them.
And Mosheh and Aharon did as the Lord commanded them, even so did they.
7:7: Moshe was eighty years old and Aharon was eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.
And Mosheh was the son of eighty years, and Aharon the son of eighty and three years, at their speaking with Pharoh.
7:8: Adonoy said to Moshe and Aharon, saying:
And the Lord spake to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
7:9: “When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Give yourselves [credibility by displaying] a marvel;’ you [Moshe] should then say to Aharon, ‘Take your rod and throw it down before Pharaoh.’ It will become a serpent.’”

When Pharoh talketh with you, saying, Give us a miracle, thou shalt say to Aharon, Take thy rod, and cast it down before Pharoh, and it shall become a basilisk-serpent; for all the inhabiters of the earth shall hear the voice of the shriek of Mizraim when I shatter them, as all the creatures heard the shriek of the serpent when made naked at the beginning.
7:10: Moshe and Aharon came to Pharaoh and they did exactly as Adonoy commanded [them]. Aharon threw his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants and it became a serpent.
And Mosheh and Aharon went in unto Pharoh, and did as the Lord had commanded. And Aharon threw down the rod before the sight of Pharoh, and before the sight of his servants, and it became a basilisk.
7:11: Pharaoh too called [his] wise men and magicians. The sorcerers of Egypt also did likewise with their magic art.
But Pharoh called the hachems and magicians; and they also, Janis and Jamberes, magicians of Mizraim, did the same by their burnings of divination.
7:12: When each man threw down his rod they (the rods) became serpents, and Aharon’s rod swallowed their rods.
They threw down each man his rod, and they became basilisks; but were forthwith changed to be what they were at first; and the rod of Aharon swallowed up their rods.
7:13: Pharaoh’s heart [remained] hard and he did not listen to [accept] them, just as Adonoy had foretold.
And the disposition Pharoh's heart was hardened, and he would not hearken to them, as the Lord had said.
7:14: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Pharaoh’s heart is heavy [unmoved]. He refuses to let the people go.
And the Lord said to Mosheh, The disposition of Pharoh's heart is obdurated in refusing to release the people.
7:15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning when he goes out to the water, and stand there to meet him by the bank of the river. The rod that was turned into a snake, take in your hand.

Go unto Pharoh in the morning: behold, he cometh forth to observe divinations at the water as a magician; so shalt thou prepare thee to meet him on the bank of the river, and Aharon's rod that was changed to be a serpent thou shalt take in thy hand.
7:16: Say to him, “Adonoy, God of the Hebrews, sent me to you to say [to you], ‘Send out My people that they may worship [before] Me in the wilderness. Behold, thus far you have not listened [accepted].
And thou shalt say to him, The Lord God of the Jehudaee hath sent me unto thee, saying Release My people, that they may serve Me in the desert; and, behold, as yet thou bast not hearkened.
7:17: This is what Adonoy has said, ‘By this you will know that I am Adonoy. Behold, with the rod that is in my hand, I will strike the water of the river and it will turn into blood.
Thus saith the Lord: By this sign thou shalt know that I am the Lord. Behold, with the rod that is in my hand, I will smite the waters of the river, and they shall be changed into blood.
7:18: The fish that is in the river will die, and the river will become polluted. The Egyptians will weary themselves [trying to purify] drinking water from the river.’”
And the fish that are in the river shall die, and the river become foul, and the Mizraee shall desist from drinking water from the river.
7:19: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Say to Aharon, ‘Take your rod and extend your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers, over their canals, over their lakes, and over every place where their water is gathered, and it [the water] will become blood. There will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, [even] in [vessels] of wood and [vessels] of stone.”

And the Lord said to Mosheh, Tell Aharon, Take thy rod and stretch forth thy hand over the waters of the Mizraee over their rivers, Over their trenches, over their canals, and over every place for collecting their waters, and they will become blood; and there shall be blood in all the land of Mizraim, and in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.
7:20: Moshe and Aharon did exactly as Adonoy commanded them. He [Aharon] lifted the rod and struck the water in the river before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his [Pharaoh’s] servants, and all the water of the river turned into blood.

And Mosheh and Aharon did so, as the Lord commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters of the river in the sight of Pharoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters of the river were turned into blood;
7:21: The fish that were in the river died, and the river became so polluted that the Egyptians were unable to drink the water from the river. There was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
and the fish that were in the river died; and the river became foul, and the Mizraee could not drink of the waters, of the river and the plague of blood was in all the land of Mizraim.
7:22: The sorcerers of Egypt did likewise with their magic art. Pharaoh’s heart remained hardened and he did not listen to [accept] them, just as Adonoy had spoken.

But so (also) did the astrologers of Mizraim by their burnings, and turned the waters of Goshen into blood. And the design of Pharoh's heart was strengthened, and he would not hearken. to them, as the Lord had said.
7:23: Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and paid no attention even to this [miracle].
And Pharoh did what was needful to him, and went unto his house, nor did he set his heart upon this plague.
7:24: The Egyptians dug around the river for water to drink, for they could not drink from the waters of the river.
And the Mizraee digged about the river for water to drink, but could not find them pure; for they were not able to drink of the water from the river.
7:25: Seven full days [passed] after Adonoy had struck the river.
And seven days were completed after the Lord had smitten the river, and the Word of the Lord had afterward healed the river.
8:1: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what Adonoy has said, “Send out my people so they may worship [before] Me.
And the Lord spoke to Mosheh, Go in unto Pharoh and say to him, Thus saith the Lord, Emancipate My people, that they may serve before Me.
8:2: If you refuse to send [them,] behold I will plague [smite] all your borders [territories] with frogs.
But if thou refuse to set them free, behold, I will plague all thy borders with frogs.
8:3: The river will swarm with frogs. They will emerge and come into your house, into your bedroom, and on your bed, into the houses of your servants and your people, into your ovens and into your kneading bowls.

And the river shall multiply frogs, and they shall ascend and come up into thy house, and into the bedchamber where thou sleepest, and upon thy couch; and into the house of thy servants, and among thy people, and into the ovens, and into thy baking-troughs,
8:4: Upon you and upon your people and upon all your servants the frogs will emerge.
and upon thy body, and upon the bodies of thy people, and upon all thy servants, shall the frogs have power.
8:5: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Say to Aharon, ‘Extend your hand with your rod over the rivers, over the streams and over the lakes, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.’”
And the Lord said to Mosheh, Lift up thy hand with thy rod over the rivers, over the trenches, and over the canals, and I will bring up the frogs upon the land of Mizraim.
8:6: Aharon extended his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frog emerged and covered the land of Egypt.

And Aharon uplifted his hand over the waters of Mizraim, and the plague of frogs came up and covered the land of Mizraim. But Mosheh (himself) did not smite the waters, either with the blood or with the frogs because through them (the waters of the Nile) he had (found) safety the time that his mother laid him in the river.
8:7: The sorcerers did likewise with their magic art, and made the frogs emerge upon the land of Egypt.
And the astrologers did likewise by their burnings, and brought up frogs upon the land of Mizraim.
8:8: Pharaoh called for Moshe and Aharon and said, “Pray to [before] Adonoy, and let Him remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send the people to sacrifice to [before] Adonoy.”

And Pharoh called to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, Pray before the Lord, that He may remove the frogs from me and from my people; and I will release the people to offer the sacrifices of a feast before the Lord.
8:9: Moshe said to Pharaoh, “Glorify [Request might for] yourself at my expense. [Exactly for] when shall I [Give me a time when I shall] pray for you, and for your servants and for your people, that the frogs be destroyed from you and from your houses, remaining only in the river.”

And Mosheh said to Pharoh, Glorify thyself on account of me. At what time dost thou request that I should pray for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, that the frogs may be destroyed from thee and from thy house, and be left only in the river?
8:10: [Pharaoh] said, “By tomorrow.” [Moshe] said, “As you say. You will then know that there is none like Adonoy, our God.
And he said, Tomorrow. And he said, According to thy word: that thou mayest know that there is none like the Lord our God.
8:11: The frogs will be removed from you, from your houses, from your servants and from your people. They will remain only in the river.
And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy house, and from thy servants, and from thy people; and those only that are in the river shall remain.
8:12: Moshe and Aharon left Pharaoh, and Moshe cried out to [prayed before] Adonoy concerning the frogs that He had set upon Pharaoh.
And Mosheh and Aharon went out from Pharoh, and Mosheh prayed before the Lord respecting the frogs, as he had proposed to Pharoh.
8:13: Adonoy did as Moshe said, the frogs died, [those that were in] the houses, the courtyards, and the fields.
And the Lord did according to the word of Mosheh; and the frogs died from the houses and from the courts and from the field,
8:14: They gathered them into [many] heaps, and the land was [they became] polluted [decayed upon the land].
and they collected them in heaps and heaps, and the land was corrupted.
8:15: [When] Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart and did not listen to [accept] them, just as Adonoy had spoken.
And Pharoh saw that he was refreshed from his molestation, but hardened his heart, and would not hearken to them, as the Lord had said.
8:16: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Say to Aharon, Extend your rod and strike the dust of the earth; and it will turn into lice throughout the whole land of Egypt.”

And the Lord said to Mosheh, Speak unto Aharon, Lift up thy rod and smite the dust of the earth, and it shall become venomous insects in all the land of Mizraim. But it shall not be by thee that the ground shall be smitten, because therein for thee was (the means of) safety when thou hadst slain the Mizraite and it received him.
8:17: They did so. Aharon extended his hand with his rod and struck the dust of the earth, and there was lice on man and beast. All the dust of the earth turned into lice throughout the whole land of Egypt.

And they did so, and Aharon lifted up his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the ground, and it became a plague of venomous insects upon the flesh of men and of cattle; all the dust of the earth was changed to become insects, in all the land of Mizraim.
8:18: The sorcerers did likewise with their magic art. They tried to bring forth lice but they could not, and there were lice on man and beast.
And the astrologers wrought with their burnings to bring forth the insects, but were not able; and the plague of insects prevailed upon men and upon cattle.
8:19: The sorcerers said to Pharaoh, “This is the finger of [a plague from before] Elohim;” but Pharaoh’s heart remained hardened and he did not listen to [accept] them, as Adonoy had spoken.

And the astrologers said to Pharoh, This is not by the power or strength of Mosheh and Aharon; but this is a plague sent from before the Lord. Yet the design of Pharoh's heart was strengthened, and he would not hearken to them, as the Lord had said.
8:20: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Rise up early in the morning and set yourself before Pharaoh, when he goes out to the water, and say to him, ‘This is what Adonoy has said, ‘Send out My people so they may worship [before] Me.

And the Lord spake to Mosheh, Arise in the morning, and stand before Pharoh: behold, be goeth forth to observe divinations at the water, as a magician; and thou shalt say to him, Thus saith the Lord, Emancipate My people, that they may worship before Me;
8:21: For if you do not send out My people, behold, I will send against you and your servants, and your nation, and your houses, swarms of wild animals. The houses of Egypt will be full of the wild animals, and so too the ground upon which they stand.

but if thou wilt not set My people free, behold, I will stir up among thee, and thy servants, and thy people, and thy house, a mixed multitude of wild beasts and the houses of the Mizraee shall be filled with a swarm of wild beasts, and they shall be upon the land also.
8:22: On that day, I will set apart the land of Goshen upon which My people stand [dwell], so that there will not be any wild animals there, so that you will know that I am Adonoy [who rules] in the midst of the earth.

And I will do wonders that day in the land of Goshen where My people dwell, that there no swarms of wild beasts shall be; - that thou mayest know that I the Lord am the Ruler in the midst of the land.
8:23: I will set a [sign of] deliverance (distinction) between [for] My people and between [but upon] your people [I will bring a plague]. This sign will take place tomorrow.”
And I will appoint redemption for My people, and upon thy people will I lay the plague: tomorrow this sign shall be.
8:24: Adonoy did so. Huge throngs of wild animals came to the house of Pharaoh and the houses of his servants. Throughout the whole land of Egypt the land was devastated by the wild animals.

And the Lord did so; and sent the mixed multitude of wild beasts in strength to the house of Pharoh, and to the house of his servants and in all the land of Mizraim the inhabitants of the land were devastated from the swarm of wild beasts.
8:25: Pharaoh called for Moshe and Aharon, and he said, “Go! Sacrifice to [before] your God [here] in the land.”
And Pharoh called to Mosheh and to Aharon., saying, Go, worship with festival sacrifices before the Lord your God in this land.
8:26: Moshe said, “It would not be proper to do so. For that which is abominable [sacred] to Egypt we intend to sacrifice to [the animal that the Egyptians worship we are taking to sacrifice before] Adonoy, our God. Could we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes and not have them stone us? [Behold, we will sacrifice the animal that the Egyptians worship, and they will see. Will they not want to stone us?]

But Mosheh said, It will not be right to do so; because we shall take sheep, which are the abomination of the Mizraee, and offer them before the Lord our God. Behold if we offer the abomination of the Mizraee before them, they would stone us with stones as an act of justice.
8:27: We must make a three day trip into the wilderness, and sacrifice to [before] Adonoy, our God, in the manner that He will tell us.”
We will go three days journey into the wilderness to offer the festival sacrifices before our God, as He hath bidden us.
8:28: Pharaoh, said, “I will send you out so that you may sacrifice to [before] Adonoy, your God in the wilderness, as long as you do not go too far away. Pray [also] for me.”
And Pharoh said, I will release you to sacrifice before the Lord your God in the wilderness, only you shall not go to a greater distance. Pray, (too,) for me.
8:29: Moshe said, “Behold, when I leave your presence I will pray to [before] Adonoy, and the wild animals will depart from Pharaoh, and from his servants and from his people, tomorrow. But let Pharaoh never again deceive us [by] refusing to send the people to sacrifice to [before] Adonoy.”

And Mosheh said, I will go forth from thee, and pray before the Lord to remove the swarm of wild beasts from Pharoh, and from his servants, and from his people, tomorrow; only let not Pharoh add to deceive, in not releasing the people to offer the festal sacrifices before the Lord.
8:30: Moshe went out from Pharaoh[’s presence] and prayed to [before] Adonoy.
And Mosheh went out from Pharoh, and prayed before the Lord;
8:31: Adonoy did as Moshe spoke [requested]. He caused the wild animals to depart from Pharaoh from his servants and from his people. Not a single one remained.
and the Lord did according to the word of the prayer of Mosheh, and removed the swarm of wild beasts from Pharoh, and from his servants, and from his people; not one was left.
8:32: But Pharaoh hardened his heart again, this time and he did not send out the people.
Yet did Pharoh strengthen the design of his heart this time also, and released not the people.
9:1: Adonoy said to Moshe, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what Adonoy, God of the Hebrews has said, Send out My people and let them serve [before] Me.
And the Lord said to Mosheh, Go in to Pharoh, and say to him, Thus saith the Lord, the God of the Jehudaee, Emancipate My people, that they may worship before Me.
9:2: For if you refuse to send them out, and continue holding them;
